_comment: Rule 3: every asset shipped from this app says where it came from and under what terms. Checked by scripts/check-asset-licenses.mjs, which requires source, licence and author on every entry. Paths are relative to this file.
_fonts: All three families are variable fonts. The files here were fetched from the Google Fonts CSS2 API with the weight axis clipped to the range this site actually sets (wght@500..700 and wght@400..700), which is why one file covers every weight of a family instead of one file per weight. Each family is split into the 'latin' and 'latin-ext' subsets Google publishes, so a browser downloads only the subset the page needs. The bytes are Google's own subsetted, hinted builds, redistributed unmodified under the OFL; the licence text is in src/styles/fonts/OFL.txt.
_generated: Two entries below name source files rather than assets. The 108 catalogue tiles (#2457) are not files: they are composed during `next build` from the vocabulary in src/lib/tiles.ts and land as inline SVG in the exported HTML, so there is no .svg or .png for the extension scan to find. Rule 3 says every asset carries a source, a licence and an author, and the answer for a generated asset is the code that generates it — not an invented provenance. check-asset-licenses.mjs checks entries as well as files, so these are enforced: their three required fields must be present and the paths they name must exist.
_share_images: The 109 share images (#2453) are the case the paragraph above did not have to answer: they ARE files — public/og/*.png, 1200x630, one per game plus one for the site. They are not tracked. `pnpm share:images` composes them from the same tile vocabulary before every build and the export copies them out, so they are build output in the way a JavaScript chunk is, and .gitignore keeps them out of the repository. Listing them individually would be 109 entries all saying the same sentence, and each would be a claim about a file no reviewer could inspect in a diff. The honest entry is the one below: the code that draws them, which is where their provenance actually lives. If they are ever committed instead of generated, check-asset-licenses.mjs will find 109 untracked-turned-tracked images and demand an entry for each, which is the right outcome — a committed image is a file somebody put there, and rule 1 wants to know where it came from.

_icons: The five app icons are drawn by scripts/make-icons.mjs — arithmetic in that file, no design tool and no third-party artwork — from the geometry of src/components/Wordmark.tsx. Re-run `node scripts/make-icons.mjs` to reproduce them byte for byte. The one departure from the wordmark is that the second seat is a ring rather than a disc, so the two seats stay distinguishable in greyscale (rule 7).
